“What is wrong? Why do you hesitate? The Holy Grail is offered in exchange. I should think the terms overwhelmingly favorable.”

The priest is right.

There is no reason for her to hesitate here.

And yet—

*I believe the path I followed—the person I have been until now—was not a mistake.*

She cannot drive those words from her mind.

pages.en:
That was the heart that loved her country—the heart of an ordinary girl before she became king.

But it was not the heart she possessed as king.

The king she became could believe in only one thing: the self who had reigned.

To deny that self would be to deny the many things she had taken from others.

—What was lost cannot be restored.

Writhing in agony, her Master continued to insist upon that truth.

The only one the king believed in was herself.

Things lost will never return…
Her master continued to appeal in his pain.

Yes. It is wrong.

She was raised as king and lived as king.

There had been no mistake in that.

Then—if destruction was the result, why had she been unable to accept it?

If she truly possessed no regret,

if she could take pride in the life she led, then she must not seek to live it again.

The tears would disappear.

The pain would disappear.

Even the cruel weight that gouged into his heart would disappear.

It would be forgiveness beyond compare: salvation of the self through erasure.

But—

if everything were made never to have happened, where would all the feelings stolen from others go?

She took many things and built her path upon many deaths.

Enduring the pain and grieving for them is itself the repose she can offer what was lost.

Therefore, if she desires to begin again, she must begin not in the past, but now.

If there is something she left undone,

she cannot return to the past and repeat it. She must begin at this moment to build the dream she failed to realize.

“Indeed. I was surprised myself. I had ordered Archer to remain hidden, yet he disobeyed me and attacked you.

“Any investigation of Archer would naturally have led back to me. I therefore had to prepare for that eventuality. You see? I did not deceive you in the least.”

It is only natural for you to discover me if you investigate Archer. Therefore, I had to come up with some sort of a plan. See? I did not lie to you at all.”

“—You are Archer's Master?”

“I am. Ten years later, history repeats itself, Saber.

“Though at the time, Kiritsugu had already defeated me, so I was not present for the final act. This is only the second time we have met—and it will be the last.”

Well, I was unable to witness the final moment since Kiritsugu had already defeated me. This will be the second and the last time I shall see you.”

pages.en:
“—Answer me. Why does Archer remain? Why did that fire break out? If Kiritsugu defeated you, why are you still alive…!?”

Saber's voice rises, seething with hatred.

…Questions she has carried for years.

It is as though she is calling him to account for the tragedy of ten years ago.

“
Answer me. Why does Archer still remain? What caused that fire? Why are you still alive even after being beaten by Kiritsugu…!?”
Saber is angry as there’s hatred in her voice.
A question long unanswered.
As if asking about the crime of the disaster ten years ago.

You saw it as well, right? The darkness that spilled out from it when you destroyed the Holy Grail. It only spilled onto Archer. Archer would not have lost his way if you had not destroyed the Holy Grail.”

“You all suffer from a remarkable poverty of imagination.

In any case, you lack imagination.
Your wishes will be granted? That is fine, but how will your wish be granted? Did you think the world would change the instant you wish?”

“How is that different? The Grail's method is perfectly rational.

“To let one person live is to kill another, is it not?

“Everything in this world rests upon equivalent exchange. If you desire an outcome that rises above the rest, you must consume something else and use it as your springboard.

“No wish can be granted if one concerns oneself with harmony.

“Change, in other words, is accomplished by plundering the weak. Surely that is the most efficient means of transformation.”

“It is. The measures the Holy Grail takes are very reasonable.
Letting one person survive means killing another.
This world is one of equal exchanges. Wishing for some special event means feeding on something to make it possible.
Wishes will not come true if you worry about harmony.
It is merely a fluctuation dependant on the plundering of the weak. It is the most efficient fluctuation.”

This man is not human.
